tasks.task_text: Font variation resources reset variation values ### Tested versions v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf] ### System information Godot v4.7.2.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1047) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600X 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.92 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description When using a font variation resource as the project's custom font under **Project > GUI > Theme > Custom Font**, the variation values will reset when adding new scripts to the project. Pretty bizarre bug https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/35e6ec2b-f798-48a9-b633-c412e905a0fa Removing the script and reloading the editor restores the custom variation values. ### Steps to reproduce This happens in a brand new project but these steps are based on the font file I used in the reproduction project. 1. Right click in the file system tab and click "New Resource" 2. Select **FontVariation** and save it as `montserrat_medium.tres` (you can name it whatever). 3. With the new variation selected, change the following: - Set the base font to `montserrat_variable_weight.ttf`. - Under Variation, click Variation Coordinates and change the weight to 600. 4. Save. 5. Go to **Project > GUI > Theme > Custom Font** and select the font variation you just created. 6. At the bottom, click **Save and Restart**. 7. Upon restart, the weight should still not have changed however creating any new scripts will trigger the variation's weight to reset. 9. Right click the file system tab and create and save a new script with any name. 10. Inspect the font variation resource and you should see the weight has been reset back to 100. 11. This will stick between editor restarts until you delete the script. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [font-variation.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31769571/font-variation.zip)

tasks.task_text: Always send an opaque buffer to interactive backends Currently, we send an RGBA buffer from Agg/Cairo up to the interactive backends. This buffer may contain non-opaque pixels. Most backends then composite this buffer onto a white background (macosx currently does not, but this is fixed in the macos rework). If we formalize this: "our interactive backends will always render onto a white background" or "our interactive backends will provide an opaque backing color to the renderer", we can instead pass up an RGBX buffer (alpha ignored, completely opaque). Depending on the backend, this may avoid a compositing operation and/or allow a less-expensive compositing operation. For example, on macOS, we could use `kCGImageAlphaNoneSkipLast` rather than `kCGImageAlphaLast` (which has to convert to premultiplied alpha). In Qt, we could use `Format_RGBX8888`. The actual performance impact of this could be hard to measure. At least in the macOS rework: actual compositing may occur at a lower level instead of our own process. That said, it seems non-ideal to hand a transparent buffer to a backend and say: "Now make this opaque" when we can instead do a `memset(ptr, 0xff, length)` at render time. Thoughts?
